originality.rationale: The genuinely new finite invariant is the nonzero order-three torsion of integral rotation coinvariants for the six-rung circular-ladder perfect-matching complex, despite a rationally regular C6 character. Agarwal–Basak establish a nonequivariant wedge classification; the most closely related published equivariant theorem explicitly assumes at least twelve rungs and computes rational lower-degree homology. Neither implies the nontrivial integral Smith factor at six rungs. Multiple exact graph-alias and equivalent lattice searches found no matching result. An inaccessible full version of the original preprint leaves residual priority risk; absence of indexed coverage is not asserted as a proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: The n=6 circular ladder is the exceptional first degree-collision of the two sphere families from the motivating homotopy classification. The integral rotation lattice becomes a natural uncomputed extension problem, not an arbitrary small parameter. Detecting Z/3 coinvariant torsion distinguishes integral modules that have identical regular rational characters and shows that equivariant integral geometry cannot be read off from ordinary wedge ranks. The exact invariant can inform the symmetry quotient and extension calculations without claiming those consequences as proved.
